symbols.name: q
symbols.def: The number of predeclared four-unit blocks.

symbols.name: j
symbols.def: The index of one of the two response-structure classes.

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: The index of a balanced assignment direction within a quadruple.

symbols.name: h_k
symbols.def: \(h_k=v_k/2\), so \(h_1,h_2,h_3\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\mathbf 1_4^\perp\).

symbols.name: E_ell
symbols.def: The coordinate embedding of \(\mathbb R^4\) into quadruple \(\ell\).

symbols.name: a
symbols.def: The larger squared-loading increment in each response geometry.

symbols.name: b
symbols.def: The smaller squared-loading increment along the shared assignment direction.

symbols.name: c_j
symbols.def: The positive squared loading attained by the class-\(j\) oracle direction.

symbols.name: s_j
symbols.def: The scale multiplying the two controllable squared-loading increments for class \(j\).

symbols.name: K_j
symbols.def: \(K_j=U_jU_j^\top\), a rank-\(q\) centered block Gram matrix.

symbols.name: x
symbols.def: A generic response vector used to define an ellipsoid.

symbols.name: M_j
symbols.def: The unit ellipsoid generated by \(K_j\), defined in \(\mathrm{def:response-classes}\).

symbols.name: Z_n
symbols.def: The assignments that use one of the six balanced sign vectors \(\{\pm v_1,\pm v_2,\pm v_3\}\) in every quadruple.

symbols.name: Pi_n
symbols.def: The convex class of blinded laws on \(\mathcal Z_n\), defined in \(\mathrm{def:design-space}\).

symbols.name: Z
symbols.def: The random assignment drawn from \(\pi\), with \(Z_i=1\) for treatment and \(Z_i=-1\) for control.

symbols.name: pi_0
symbols.def: The product law that independently chooses each of \(\pm v_1,\pm v_2,\pm v_3\) with probability \(1/6\) in every quadruple.

symbols.name: pi_sh
symbols.def: The product law that independently chooses \(v_3\) or \(-v_3\) with probability \(1/2\) in every quadruple.

symbols.name: Y_i(0)
symbols.def: The fixed outcome for unit \(i\) under control.

symbols.name: Y_i(1)
symbols.def: The fixed outcome for unit \(i\) under treatment.

symbols.name: RE_j
symbols.def: \(\operatorname{RE}_j(\pi)=r_j^\star/R_j(\pi)\), the exact variance ratio used in Ryan--Esserman--Li equation (8).

symbols.name: J_gen
symbols.def: The number of classes in the higher-rank extension.

symbols.name: K_j_gen
symbols.def: A menu of known block-supported centered Gram matrices with block rank exceeding one allowed.

symbols.name: lambda_gen_star
symbols.def: The gain-normalized commitment value obtained by replacing \(K_1,K_2\) with \(\{K_j^{\mathrm{gen}}:1\le j\le J_{\mathrm{gen}}\}\).

symbols.name: H_mat
symbols.def: The trace-relaxation and matrix-discrepancy route defined in \(\mathrm{def:matrix-discrepancy-handle}\).

assumptions.condition: The schedule \(\{Y_i(0),Y_i(1):1\le i\le n\}\) is fixed before treatment assignment.
For each unit \(i\), the observed outcome under assignment \(Z\) equals \(Y_i(1)\) when \(Z_i=1\) and equals \(Y_i(0)\) when \(Z_i=-1\).
Conditional on the fixed potential outcomes and the design-stage Gram matrices, \(Z\) has law \(\pi\).
A candidate member \(x\) of class \(j\) satisfies \(x\in\operatorname{range}(K_j)\).
A candidate member \(x\) of class \(j\) satisfies \(x^\top K_j^\dagger x\le1\).

definitions.name: quadruple_balanced_assignment_set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal Z_n=\{z\in\{-1,1\}^n:z_{[\ell]}\in\{\pm v_1,\pm v_2,\pm v_3\}\text{ for every }\ell=1,\ldots,q\}\).

definitions.name: block_complete_randomization
definitions.construction: Under \(\pi_0\), the block assignments are independent and each element of \(\{\pm v_1,\pm v_2,\pm v_3\}\) has probability \(1/6\).

definitions.name: shared_direction_product_randomization
definitions.construction: Under \(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}}\), independently across \(\ell\), set \(Z_{[\ell]}=\varepsilon_\ell v_3\) with \(\Pr(\varepsilon_\ell=1)=\Pr(\varepsilon_\ell=-1)=1/2\).

definitions.name: block_response_ellipsoids
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_j=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:x\in\operatorname{range}(K_j),\ x^\top K_j^\dagger x\le1\},\quad j\in\{1,2\}\).

definitions.name: assignment_covariance_score_matrix_and_class_risk
definitions.construction: For \(\pi\in\Pi_n\), set \(Q_\pi=\mathbb E_\pi[ZZ^\top]\), \(C_j(\pi)=U_j^\top Q_\pi U_j\), \(V_\pi(x)=n^{-2}x^\top Q_\pi x\), and \(R_j(\pi)=\sup_{x\in\mathcal M_j}V_\pi(x)\).

definitions.name: exact_ryan_esserman_li_variance_ratio
definitions.construction: For each response scenario \(j\), set \(\operatorname{RE}_j(\pi)=r_j^\star/R_j(\pi)\) and \(\eta_{\mathrm{REL}}=\max_{\pi\in\Pi_n}\min_{j\in\{1,2\}}\operatorname{RE}_j(\pi)\). This is equation (8) and Algorithm 1's maximin operation after mapping \(\sigma_j^{2*}\) to \(r_j^\star\) and \(\sigma_j^2(\pi)\) to \(R_j(\pi)\).

definitions.name: higher_rank_matrix_discrepancy_handle
definitions.construction: Start from the normalized trace relaxation for the menu \(\{K_j^{\mathrm{gen}}:1\le j\le J_{\mathrm{gen}}\}\), then use blockwise balanced matrix discrepancy and noncommutative spectral concentration to construct a blinded assignment law whose class score second moments approach the relaxation simultaneously. The relaxation gap and the attaining law are the objects to be derived.

statements.statement: For every \(\pi\in\Pi_n\), \(\widehat\tau-\tau_N=n^{-1}Z^\top\mu\), \(\mathbb E_\pi[\widehat\tau]=\tau_N\), and \(\operatorname{Var}_\pi(\widehat\tau)=V_\pi(\mu)=n^{-2}\mu^\top Q_\pi\mu\). For each \(j\in\{1,2\}\), \[R_j(\pi)=n^{-2}\lambda_{\max}(K_j^{1/2}Q_\pi K_j^{1/2})=n^{-2}\lambda_{\max}\{C_j(\pi)\}.\] Consequently, \(\mu\in\mathcal M_j\) implies \(\operatorname{Var}_\pi(\widehat\tau)\le R_j(\pi)\).
statements.justification: This identifies the exact finite-population causal variance and the observable eigenvalue that certifies every subsequent design comparison.
statements.gap: Kallus gives the single-class covariance-risk representation; the lemma specializes it to the block score matrices used by the quantitative two-class frontier.
statements.consumer: A trial auditor can compute each declared worst-case variance from the design-stage Gram matrix and the published assignment law.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(\pi\in\Pi_n\).  Every \(z\in\mathcal Z_n\) is balanced within every quadruple, hence \(z^\top\mathbf 1_n=0\).  By \(\texttt{def:estimator}\) and consistency in \(\texttt{ass:no-interference}\), for each unit
\[
2Z_iY_i^{\mathrm{obs}}
=Z_i\{(1+Z_i)Y_i(1)+(1-Z_i)Y_i(0)\}
=Y_i(1)-Y_i(0)+Z_i\{Y_i(1)+Y_i(0)\}.
\]
Summing, dividing by \(n\), and using \(Z^\top\mathbf 1_n=0\) gives
\[
\widehat\tau-\tau_N
=n^{-1}Z^\top\{Y(1)+Y(0)\}
=n^{-1}Z^\top P_n\{Y(1)+Y(0)\}
=n^{-1}Z^\top\mu. \tag{1}
\]
The potential-outcome schedule is fixed by \(\texttt{ass:fixed-potential-outcomes}\), and assignment is the only randomness by \(\texttt{ass:assignment-only-randomness}\).  Moreover, the blinding identity \(\pi(z)=\pi(-z)\) from \(\texttt{def:design-space}\) implies
\[
\mathbb E_\pi Z=\sum_{z\in\mathcal Z_n}z\pi(z)=0. \tag{2}
\]
Thus (1)--(2) yield \(\mathbb E_\pi\widehat\tau=\tau_N\).  Since \(Q_\pi=\mathbb E_\pi[ZZ^\top]\), they also yield
\[
\operatorname{Var}_\pi(\widehat\tau)
=n^{-2}\mathbb E_\pi[(Z^\top\mu)^2]
=n^{-2}\mu^\top Q_\pi\mu
=V_\pi(\mu). \tag{3}
\]
No assignment-probability inverse is used; the boundary designs in \(\Pi_n\) are therefore allowed.  Blinding nevertheless gives treatment probability \(1/2\) to every unit.

It remains to compute the ellipsoidal supremum.  Fix \(j\).  The declared rank condition \(\operatorname{rank}(K_j)=q\), together with \(K_j=U_jU_j^\top\) and the fact that \(U_j\) has \(q\) columns, implies that \(U_j\) has full column rank.  Its polar decomposition is
\[
U_j=W_jH_j,\qquad W_j^\top W_j=I_q,qquad H_j=(U_j^\top U_j)^{1/2}\succ0. \tag{4}
\]
Consequently,
\[
K_j=W_jH_j^2W_j^\top,qquad
K_j^\dagger=W_jH_j^{-2}W_j^\top. \tag{5}
\]
Every \(x\in\operatorname{range}(K_j)=\operatorname{range}(U_j)\) has a unique representation \(x=U_j\beta\).  Equations (4)--(5) show
\[
x^\top K_j^\dagger x
=\beta^\top H_jW_j^\top W_jH_j^{-2}W_j^\top W_jH_j\beta
=\|\beta\|_2^2. \tag{6}
\]
Thus \(\texttt{def:response-classes}\) gives
\[
\mathcal M_j=\{U_j\beta:\|\beta\|_2\le1\}. \tag{7}
\]
The Rayleigh--Ritz identity, applied to the positive-semidefinite matrix \(C_j(\pi)=U_j^\top Q_\pi U_j\), now gives
\[
R_j(\pi)
=n^{-2}\sup_{\|\beta\|_2\le1}\beta^\top C_j(\pi)\beta
=n^{-2}\lambda_{\max}\{C_j(\pi)\}. \tag{8}
\]
Also, (4) gives
\[
K_j^{1/2}Q_\pi K_j^{1/2}
=W_j\{H_jW_j^\top Q_\pi W_jH_j\}W_j^\top,
\qquad
C_j(\pi)=H_jW_j^\top Q_\pi W_jH_j. \tag{9}
\]
The matrix on the left of (9) is the orthogonal embedding by \(W_j\) of the matrix on the right, with zeros on the orthogonal complement.  Their largest eigenvalues therefore agree.  This proves both spectral identities.  Finally, if \(\mu\in\mathcal M_j\), then (3) and the definition of the supremum in \(R_j\) give \(\operatorname{Var}_\pi(\widehat\tau)=V_\pi(\mu)\le R_j(\pi)\), as claimed.

statements.statement: For every finite \(q\ge1\) and the two-class menu in \(\mathrm{def:block-geometry}\), \[r_j^\star=\frac{4c_j}{n^2},\qquad B_j=\frac{4}{n^2}\left(c_j+\frac{s_j(a+b)}{3}\right),\qquad \Delta_j=\frac{4s_j(a+b)}{3n^2}.\] For every \(\pi\in\Pi_n\), the observable score matrices obey the sharp spectral lower certificate \[\lambda_{\max}\{C_1(\pi)\}\ge\frac{\operatorname{tr}C_1(\pi)}q=4\{c_1+s_1(ap_2(\pi)+bp_3(\pi))\},\] \[\lambda_{\max}\{C_2(\pi)\}\ge\frac{\operatorname{tr}C_2(\pi)}q=4\{c_2+s_2(ap_1(\pi)+bp_3(\pi))\}.\] These inequalities and \(a>2b>0\) imply the exact finite-sample commitment frontier \[\lambda^\star=\frac{a-2b}{a+b}.\] The product law \(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}}\) attains equality in both spectral certificates, is therefore minimax, and strictly improves on block complete randomization for both classes: \(R_j(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}})=4(c_j+s_jb)/n^2<B_j\). The displayed trace lower bound and the matching eigenvalue of \(C_j(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}})\) form a finite-\(n\) optimality certificate using only the known Gram matrices and the committed assignment law.
statements.justification: The theorem gives an exact, nonasymptotic price of committing across two incompatible response structures and supplies the implementable law and matching spectral certificate.
statements.gap: Kallus optimizes one response class, while generic maximin equivalence theorems characterize scalarization; neither derives this quantitative causal commitment frontier or its sharp block-score eigenvalue bound.
statements.consumer: A trial organized in matched quadruples can randomize once along the declared shared contrast and guarantee exactly the stated fraction of each prognostic model's available variance reduction.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(q\ge1\).  The conditions \(c_j>0\) and \(s_j>0\), and the disjoint block supports, ensure that every \(U_j\) has rank \(q\); all eigenvalues and divisions below are therefore well defined.  For a block \(\ell\), write
\[
d_{1,1}=c_1,\quad d_{1,2}=c_1+s_1a,\quad d_{1,3}=c_1+s_1b,
\]
\[
d_{2,1}=c_2+s_2a,\quad d_{2,2}=c_2,\quad d_{2,3}=c_2+s_2b. \tag{1}
\]
Because \(h_k=v_k/2\) and the \(h_k\)'s are orthonormal, whenever \(Z_{[\ell]}=\varepsilon v_k\), with \(\varepsilon\in\{-1,1\}\),
\[
u_{j\ell}^\top Z=2\varepsilon\sqrt{d_{j,k}},
\qquad
(u_{j\ell}^\top Z)^2=4d_{j,k}. \tag{2}
\]
No independence across blocks is needed for (2).  Since \(C_j(\pi)=\mathbb E_\pi[(U_j^\top Z)(U_j^\top Z)^\top]\), summing its diagonal entries and using \(\texttt{def:direction-frequencies}\) gives
\[
\frac{\operatorname{tr}C_1(\pi)}q
=4\{c_1+s_1(ap_2(\pi)+bp_3(\pi))\}, \tag{3}
\]
\[
\frac{\operatorname{tr}C_2(\pi)}q
=4\{c_2+s_2(ap_1(\pi)+bp_3(\pi))\}. \tag{4}
\]
The matrix \(C_j(\pi)\) is positive semidefinite and has dimension \(q\).  If its eigenvalues are \(\rho_1\ge\cdots\ge\rho_q\ge0\), then \(\rho_1\ge q^{-1}\sum_{\ell=1}^q\rho_\ell\).  Equations (3)--(4) therefore prove the two displayed spectral lower certificates.

Because \(p_1+p_2+p_3=1\) and all frequencies are nonnegative, (3)--(4), together with \(\texttt{lem:variance-and-spectral-risk}\), imply \(R_j(\pi)\ge4c_j/n^2\).  For class \(1\), take independent Rademacher signs on direction \(v_1\) in every block.  Then the block scores in (2) are independent, centered, and have squared magnitude \(4c_1\), so \(C_1=4c_1I_q\).  The analogous design on \(v_2\) gives \(C_2=4c_2I_q\).  Both laws belong to \(\Pi_n\).  Hence the lower bounds are attained and
\[
r_j^\star=\frac{4c_j}{n^2}. \tag{5}
\]
Under \(\pi_0\), every local direction has probability \(1/3\), independent signs center the block scores, and different blocks are independent.  Thus
\[
C_j(\pi_0)=4\left\{c_j+\frac{s_j(a+b)}3\right\}I_q. \tag{6}
\]
Equations (5)--(6) and the spectral-risk lemma give
\[
B_j=\frac4{n^2}\left\{c_j+\frac{s_j(a+b)}3\right\},
\qquad
\Delta_j=\frac{4s_j(a+b)}{3n^2}>0. \tag{7}
\]
The positivity in (7) uses \(s_j>0\) and \(a+b>0\), so gain normalization is legitimate.

We next certify the commitment optimum.  Suppress the argument \(\pi\) and put
\[
L_1=ap_2+bp_3,qquad L_2=ap_1+bp_3,qquad A=a+b. \tag{8}
\]
The trace certificates, (7), and the definition of \(g_j\) imply
\[
g_1(\pi)\le1-\frac{3L_1}{A},
\qquad
g_2(\pi)\le1-\frac{3L_2}{A}. \tag{9}
\]
Moreover,
\[
\max(L_1,L_2)
\ge\frac{L_1+L_2}{2}
=\frac a2(1-p_3)+bp_3
=b+\left(\frac a2-b\right)(1-p_3)
\ge b, \tag{10}
\]
where the last inequality uses the primitive boundary condition \(a>2b\) and \(0\le p_3\le1\).  Combining (9)--(10), every feasible law obeys
\[
\min_{j\in\{1,2\}}g_j(\pi)
\le1-\frac{3b}{a+b}
=\frac{a-2b}{a+b}. \tag{11}
\]
Under \(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}}\), (2) and independent signs give
\[
C_j(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}})=4(c_j+s_jb)I_q,qquad
R_j(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}})=\frac{4(c_j+s_jb)}{n^2}. \tag{12}
\]
Thus both inequalities in (9) are equalities with \(p_3=1\), and each gain fraction equals the right side of (11).  The matching upper and lower bounds prove
\[
\lambda^\star=\frac{a-2b}{a+b}, \tag{13}
\]
and (3)--(4), together with (12), are the asserted finite-sample optimality certificate.  In fact, equality in (10) requires \(p_3=1\), because \(a/2-b>0\); hence every gain-normalized optimizer has \(p_3=1\).  Finally,
\[
B_j-R_j(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}})
=\frac{4s_j}{n^2}\left(\frac{a+b}{3}-b\right)
=\frac{4s_j(a-2b)}{3n^2}>0, \tag{14}
\]
which proves strict improvement.

For the required smallest-instance check, take \(q=1\), so \(n=4\).  A blinded law assigns total masses \(p_1,p_2,p_3\) to the three pairs \(\{\pm v_k\}\).  The score matrix is then scalar, so (3)--(4) are equalities for every one of the six assignments and every mixture of them.  Direct enumeration gives \(p_k=1/3\) for \(\pi_0\), \(p_3=1\) for \(\pi_{\mathrm{sh}}\), and exactly (5)--(14).  At the excluded boundary \(a=2b\), the strict coefficient in (10) vanishes and the strict improvement in (14) disappears; thus the stated boundary condition is load bearing rather than cosmetic.

statements.statement: Embed the menu as the two-scenario maximin variance subproblem of Ryan, Esserman, and Li (2023, equation (8) and Algorithm 1) by setting \(\sigma_j^{2*}=r_j^\star\) and \(\sigma_j^2(\pi)=R_j(\pi)\). Then their exact component criterion is \(\operatorname{RE}_j(\pi)=r_j^\star/R_j(\pi)\). If \(\kappa_2>\kappa_1\), its maximin value on the same implementable design space is \[\eta_{\mathrm{REL}}=\left[1+\frac{ab\kappa_1\kappa_2}{\kappa_1(a-b)+\kappa_2b}\right]^{-1}.\] Every relative-efficiency optimizer has average direction frequencies \[p_1=0,\qquad p_2=\frac{b(\kappa_2-\kappa_1)}{\kappa_1(a-b)+\kappa_2b},\qquad p_3=1-p_2,\] and an independent-block, independent-sign law with these frequencies attains the value. Every gain-normalized commitment optimizer instead has \(p_3=1\). Hence the optimizer sets are disjoint for the open parameter region \(a>2b>0\) and \(\kappa_2>\kappa_1>0\), even though both criteria use the same two oracle variances, committed variances, and feasible balanced assignment laws.
statements.justification: The exact shared-subproblem calculation shows that baseline-gain retention answers a different design promise than the published oracle-variance ratio.
statements.gap: Ryan, Esserman, and Li define relative efficiency by equation (8) and maximize its worst scenario in Algorithm 1; they do not analyze the fraction of improvement over a common randomized baseline or the resulting stable optimizer separation.
statements.consumer: A planner can decide whether the operational promise is protection of oracle-relative efficiency or protection of each model's attainable improvement over the routine randomization baseline.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{thm:quadruple-menu-frontier}\), \(r_j^\star=4c_j/n^2\).  The exact component criterion in \(\texttt{def:ryan-relative-efficiency}\) is therefore the stated ratio \(\operatorname{RE}_j(\pi)=r_j^\star/R_j(\pi)\); no identification or asymptotic substitution is being made.  The spectral certificates in that theorem imply, with \(p_k=p_k(\pi)\),
\[
\operatorname{RE}_1(\pi)
\le\frac1{1+F_1},qquad
\operatorname{RE}_2(\pi)
\le\frac1{1+F_2}, \tag{1}
\]
where
\[
F_1=\kappa_1(ap_2+bp_3),qquad
F_2=\kappa_2(ap_1+bp_3). \tag{2}
\]
All denominators are positive because \(c_j,s_j,a,b>0\).  Hence maximizing the worst upper bound in (1) is equivalent to minimizing \(\max(F_1,F_2)\) on the frequency simplex.

Assume \(\kappa_2>\kappa_1>0\), and define
\[
D=\kappa_1(a-b)+\kappa_2b,qquad
\alpha=\frac{\kappa_2b}{D},qquad
1-\alpha=\frac{\kappa_1(a-b)}D. \tag{3}
\]
Since \(a>2b>0\), one has \(D>0\) and \(0<\alpha<1\).  Substituting \(p_3=1-p_1-p_2\) into (2) and simplifying gives the global affine certificate
\[
\begin{aligned}
\alpha F_1+(1-\alpha)F_2
&=\frac{ab\kappa_1\kappa_2}{D}
+\frac{a(a-2b)\kappa_1\kappa_2}{D}p_1\\
&\ge \frac{ab\kappa_1\kappa_2}{D}=:m. 
\end{aligned} \tag{4}
\]
Because a maximum dominates every convex combination, (4) proves \(\max(F_1,F_2)\ge m\).

Equality is feasible.  Set
\[
p_1^\circ=0,qquad
p_2^\circ=\frac{b(\kappa_2-\kappa_1)}D,qquad
p_3^\circ=1-p_2^\circ. \tag{5}
\]
The numerator in \(p_2^\circ\) is positive, while
\[
D-b(\kappa_2-\kappa_1)=a\kappa_1>0, \tag{6}
\]
so (5) lies in the simplex.  Direct substitution yields \(F_1=F_2=m\).  Construct a law that, independently in every block, chooses direction \(k\) with probability \(p_k^\circ\) and then multiplies it by an independent Rademacher sign.  This law belongs to \(\Pi_n\).  Its block scores are centered and independent, and their second moments are identical across blocks; consequently
\[
C_j=4c_j(1+F_j)I_q,qquad
R_j=\frac{4c_j}{n^2}(1+F_j). \tag{7}
\]
Thus (1) is attained for both classes, and (4)--(7) prove
\[
\eta_{\mathrm{REL}}
=\frac1{1+m}
=\left[1+\frac{ab\kappa_1\kappa_2}{\kappa_1(a-b)+\kappa_2b}\right]^{-1}. \tag{8}
\]

The certificate also proves the asserted uniqueness of average frequencies.  If any design attains (8), then both inequalities
\[
\min_j\operatorname{RE}_j(\pi)
\le\{1+\max(F_1,F_2)\}^{-1}
\le(1+m)^{-1} \tag{9}
\]
must be equalities.  Equality in (4) forces \(p_1=0\), since its coefficient is strictly positive.  Equality between a maximum and the strictly interior convex combination in (4) forces \(F_1=F_2=m\).  Solving this equality on the face \(p_1=0\) yields exactly (5).  Hence every relative-efficiency optimizer has the displayed average frequencies.

For the gain-normalized problem, the proof of \(\texttt{thm:quadruple-menu-frontier}\) showed
\[
\max\{ap_2+bp_3,ap_1+bp_3\}
\ge b+\left(\frac a2-b\right)(1-p_3). \tag{10}
\]
Attaining its commitment value requires equality with \(b\), and \(a/2-b>0\) forces \(p_3=1\).  In contrast, (5) has \(p_2^\circ>0\) whenever \(\kappa_2>\kappa_1\).  The two optimizer sets are therefore disjoint throughout the stated open parameter region.  Both witnesses are blinded block-balanced laws on precisely the same finite support, so the separation is caused by the normalization criterion and not by a change of feasible designs.

statements.statement: If the design criterion is restricted to class \(1\), the product law using independent signs on local direction \(v_1\) attains \(R_1=4c_1/n^2=r_1^\star\); if it is restricted to class \(2\), the analogous law on \(v_2\) attains \(R_2=4c_2/n^2=r_2^\star\). Thus either one-class commitment problem has value \(1\), while the two-class value is strictly smaller than \(1\).
statements.justification: This recovers the known single-class oracle boundary and isolates the loss caused only by response-structure uncertainty.
statements.gap: The one-class equality is a validation reduction, not a novelty claim.
statements.consumer: The reduction lets users verify that the new criterion agrees with established minimax balance when only one prognostic structure is credible.
statements.proof_tex:
Consider class \(1\).  Under the product law that assigns \(Z_{[\ell]}=\varepsilon_\ell v_1\) with independent Rademacher signs, orthonormality of the \(h_k\)'s gives
\[
u_{1\ell}^\top Z=2\varepsilon_\ell\sqrt{c_1}.
\]
The scores are independent and centered across blocks, so \(C_1=4c_1I_q\).  The spectral-risk identity then gives \(R_1=4c_1/n^2\), which equals \(r_1^\star\) by \(\texttt{thm:quadruple-menu-frontier}\).  Replacing \(v_1,c_1\) by \(v_2,c_2\) gives \(C_2=4c_2I_q\) and \(R_2=4c_2/n^2=r_2^\star\) for class \(2\).  Both laws are in \(\Pi_n\), including at every finite \(q\ge1\), because independent symmetric signs imply \(\pi(z)=\pi(-z)\).

For either single class, \(R_j(\pi)\ge r_j^\star\) for every feasible design by the definition of the oracle minimum.  Since \(\Delta_j>0\), this implies \(g_j(\pi)\le1\), while the displayed oracle law attains \(g_j=1\).  Thus each one-class commitment value is exactly \(1\).  For both classes together, \(\texttt{thm:quadruple-menu-frontier}\) gives
\[
\lambda^\star=\frac{a-2b}{a+b}.
\]
The conditions \(a>2b>0\) imply \(0<\lambda^\star<1\), proving that the loss relative to the one-class boundary is caused by simultaneous response-structure uncertainty.

statements.statement: For \(J_{\mathrm{gen}}\ge3\) block-supported response classes with noncommuting within-block Gram matrices \(K_j^{\mathrm{gen}}\), characterize necessary and sufficient spectral conditions under which the normalized trace relaxation equals \(\lambda_{\mathrm{gen}}^\star\). When equality fails, determine the sharp finite-\(n\) integrality gap and construct from \(\mathcal H_{\mathrm{mat}}\) a blinded block-balanced law attaining that gap up to the optimal constant.
statements.justification: The rank-one menu makes the trace certificate exact; the open problem asks when that phenomenon survives genuinely matrix-valued and multi-class response uncertainty.
statements.gap: Harshaw et al. control one chosen feature geometry, and Kallus optimizes one chosen response class; neither gives a sharp simultaneous-oracle spectral relaxation gap for several noncommuting Gram matrices.
statements.consumer: A platform carrying several linear and nonlinear prognostic kernels could determine whether a single launch-time blocked randomization has a certifiable simultaneous gain guarantee.

sampling_model.design: A finite population of size \(n=4q\) is partitioned before assignment into \(q\) matched quadruples. The experimenter commits to a blinded probability law supported on assignments with two treated and two control units in every quadruple.
sampling_model.units: The units have fixed potential-outcome pairs \(Y_i(0),Y_i(1)\), fixed block membership, and two design-stage response Gram matrices \(K_1,K_2\).
sampling_model.treatment: Within each quadruple the local assignment is one of \(\pm v_1,\pm v_2,\pm v_3\); therefore every realized assignment has exactly \(n/2\) treated units.
sampling_model.overlap: Global blinding \(\pi(z)=\pi(-z)\) gives marginal treatment probability \(1/2\) for every unit, and exact balance holds within every predeclared quadruple.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no superpopulation nuisance estimation. The block partition, response Gram matrices, and spectral parameters are fixed and observable at design time; the potential outcomes remain fixed and unobserved at assignment.
sampling_model.causal_interpretation: The only randomness is \(Z\sim\pi\). The difference in means is design-unbiased for the finite-population average treatment effect, and each risk bound is conditional on the fixed schedule.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Equation (8) defines relative efficiency as oracle variance divided by the candidate-design variance, and Algorithm 1 maximizes the smallest relative efficiency over the parameter grid.
Theorem 1 links worst-case mean-squared error for one response-function class to its balance criterion and derives the corresponding minimax design problem.
The paper characterizes minimax randomization for one specified response class through the assignment covariance and emphasizes genuinely mixed optimal designs.
Theorem 3 gives the established equivalence between maximin component efficiency and a Bayesian criterion supported on binding objectives.
The Gram--Schmidt Walk controls covariance and discrepancy for one chosen feature geometry.

tldr: For \(n=4q\) units randomized within matched quadruples, two rank-\(q\) response ellipsoids have different oracle assignment directions but share a third near-oracle direction. The main theorem derives the exact finite-sample commitment frontier \(\lambda^\star=(a-2b)/(a+b)\): an observable trace lower bound on each class score matrix upper-bounds every law's guarantee, and independent random signs on the shared direction attain the bound while strictly reducing both class risks relative to block complete randomization. A second theorem embeds the same two-scenario variance problem into Ryan--Esserman--Li's exact equation (8) relative-efficiency criterion and proves that its optimizer is disjoint on an open parameter region. Generic maximin saddle equivalence is prior method, not a contribution. The open question asks when the trace certificate remains sharp for higher-rank, noncommuting kernel menus.

project_justification.gap: Single-class causal randomization results determine one response-class oracle, and general multi-objective design results provide established saddle and binding-weight technology. They do not give a quantitative finite-population price for committing across response geometries, a matching observable spectral certificate, or a direct comparison with the exact published relative-efficiency formula.
project_justification.niche: Matched-quadruple experiments provide a nontrivial implementable setting in which incompatible class oracles, a shared safe assignment, and the full randomization law can all be analyzed without asymptotics or a relaxation-only design.
project_justification.fill: The project derives the exact finite-\(n\) frontier \(\lambda^\star=(a-2b)/(a+b)\), proves sharpness through matching trace and eigenvalue bounds, supplies the attaining block-balanced law, establishes strict improvement over block complete randomization for both classes, and proves stable nonrepresentability against Ryan--Esserman--Li equation (8) on the same two-scenario variance subproblem.

related_work: Kallus (2018, Theorem 1 and Sections 1 and 7) makes a response-function class the primitive of a minimax balancing problem. Kallus (2021, Sections 1 and 4--6) shows why the optimizer for one class is generally a mixed assignment law characterized through covariance. These papers inform the class risk and the one-class reduction; the new theorem instead computes the exact loss from one commitment across a specified two-class menu. Proposition 1 gives the one-class oracle boundary without claiming a sharper single-class result. Ryan, Esserman, and Li (2023, Section 3.2, equation (8), and Algorithm 1) are the exact criterion comparator. Their equation is \(\operatorname{RE}_{\mathrm{HTE}}=\sigma_{\mathrm{HTE}}^{2*}/\sigma_{\mathrm{HTE}}^2\), and Algorithm 1 instructs the user to identify the scenario with the "smallest RE" and then choose the design with the "largest RE" among those minima. Theorem 2 maps these two variances to the class oracle and committed risks on the same two-scenario design problem and proves that this published rule and baseline-gain retention have disjoint optimizers on an open parameter region. Tommasi, Rodr\'iguez-D\'iaz, and L\'opez-Fidalgo (2023, Theorem 3) already establish the generic maximin binding-weight equivalence. That result is methodological background only; no abstract saddle theorem is claimed here. Harshaw, S\"avje, Spielman, and Zhang (2024, Sections 1, 8, and 9) provide covariance and discrepancy tools for one feature geometry, which motivate the matrix-discrepancy handle for the higher-rank open question. Bai (2023, Theorem 2.1) supplies the permutation-invariant complete-randomization benchmark but does not address the structured two-geometry commitment price.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact frontier uses a deliberately structured rank-\(q\) menu with identical four-unit geometry across predeclared blocks. The trace certificate need not be sharp for higher-rank noncommuting block kernels, and resolving that integrality gap is the explicit open question. The generic saddle or binding-weight equivalence is established by Tommasi, Rodr\'iguez-D\'iaz, and L\'opez-Fidalgo (2023, Theorem 3) and carries no novelty claim.
honest_scope: The theorem targets are the finite-population variance identity, the exact two-class frontier, the matching implementable design and spectral certificate, the strict improvement over block complete randomization, and the exact separation from Ryan--Esserman--Li relative efficiency. The higher-rank, noncommuting menu frontier remains open. Deleting either response class recovers the established one-class oracle value \(1\). No asymptotic limit law, universal kernel-menu rate, unrestricted global-balance theorem, or polynomial-time solver is claimed.
